1. **Review** — walk the `in-review` set (5a3d152c, 3d952036, 5b3da351, f9e70385, d7141fac, 0c02b304) against their acceptance criteria before closing any of them.
2. **Validate live via the structured ticket entities themselves** — dogfood: use part-addressed writes/freeze/projected-read transports on real tickets (not just the scratch ticket used for first-pass proof) to confirm the review step above.

## Review Summary — Structured Ticket Entities fix chain (6 in-review tickets)

**Scope verified:** code reading (filesystem.rs, ticket.rs, parts.rs, schema_registry.rs, schema.rs, store.rs, store/parts.rs, store/lifecycle.rs, store/query.rs, ticket_fs.rs, manifest_format.rs, ticket-mcp/ticket-http/ticket-cli transport types), `cargo build --workspace`, `cargo test -p ticket-api`, `cargo test -p ticket-mcp`, live MCP dogfooding on real store tickets plus one disposable scratch ticket (created and deleted within this session, not part of the reviewed set).

### Validation commands run

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo build --workspace` | Success, warnings only |
| `cargo test -p ticket-api` | 154 lib + 1 + 1 + 4 integration passed, 0 failed (154 vs. tickets' claimed 143–154 across sessions — consistent with incremental additions) |
| `cargo test -p ticket-mcp` | All suites passed, **including** `update_ticket_blocked_transition_reports_recovery_fields`, which d7141fac's evidence claims is a pre-existing failure — it is not failing now |
| `grep -rl 'state = "new"' .ticket/tickets memory-api/.ticket/tickets` / same for `"ready"` | 2 hits, both inside `description.md` prose (one is 5b3da351's own description discussing the migration), zero in actual `ticket.toml` state fields — migration is clean |
| MCP dogfood: `update_ticket` with `description`, no `description_mode`, against [0c02b304](memory-api/.ticket/tickets/0c02b304-de04-4e29-818f-fb1e6797bdc0/ticket.toml) | Rejected with the exact documented error naming both modes; ticket unchanged |
| MCP dogfood: `list_parts` on real `planned` tickets 3a1ec9f8, c2d6a14a, and [d7141fac](memory-api/.ticket/tickets/d7141fac-8c1f-42c9-a392-7e400bb5f2ba/ticket.toml) | All show `frozen: false` on their (implicit) objective part despite being in `planned` state |
| MCP dogfood on disposable scratch ticket (created → transitioned to `planned` → probed → deleted, not part of reviewed set): `write_part` targeting the now-frozen objective | **Correctly rejected** with `FrozenPartWrite` and full recovery text |
| Same scratch ticket: `update_ticket(description=..., description_mode=replace)` while objective part was `frozen: true` | **Succeeded** (`description_updated: true`) — bypassed the freeze gate entirely |

---

### 🔴 Critical cross-cutting finding: the freeze gate has a live bypass

`TicketStore::update`'s legacy whole-description write path ([store.rs L655-700](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store.rs#L655-L700)) calls `TicketFs::write_description` directly and **never calls `enforce_part_write_gate`**. Confirmed live: on a scratch ticket with a materialized, `frozen: true` objective part, `write_part` correctly rejected the write, but `update_ticket(description=..., description_mode="replace")` on the *same ticket in the same state* succeeded, writing a divergent `description.md` while the real frozen `parts/<uuid>.md` objective was left untouched — a split-brain condition (`get_ticket_description` now returns different content than `get_part` for the "same" objective).

This directly contradicts f9e70385's AC7 ("there is no alternate write entry point that can touch frozen content without the state-transition path") and reproduces the *shape* of the original corruption incident (divergent content via an untyped write path) that this entire epic exists to prevent. It affects every ticket in this chain that relies on the freeze guarantee: **f9e70385, 3d952036, d7141fac**.

Separately (lower severity, and apparently anticipated): real `planned` tickets already in the store today (3a1ec9f8, c2d6a14a, and d7141fac itself) show `frozen: false` because freeze only fires on a state *transition*, not retroactively. A migration validation spec (`vt-structured-ticket-entities-migration`, linked to ticket f65f2b32, **not in this review batch**) explicitly anticipates "tickets already in `planned` must be migrated via unfreeze then re-freeze" — so this gap is tracked, just not yet closed, and not disclosed in any of the six tickets under review.

---

### 🟠 Second cross-cutting finding: silent history-append swallowing is fixed in one place, not eliminated

0c02b304 claims to fix "silent history-append failures" and states "Not satisfied: None." Verified: the fix (`if let Err(error) = ... { tracing::error!(...) }`) is real and correct at [store.rs L543](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store.rs#L543) (the `update_ticket` path). But `let _ = TicketFs::append_history(...)` — the exact discarded-Result pattern being "fixed" — still exists at 8 other call sites in the same crate:
- [store.rs L302](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store.rs#L302) (ticket creation)
- [store/lifecycle.rs L262](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store/lifecycle.rs#L262) (attach)
- [store/parts.rs L94, L137, L198](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store/parts.rs) (`write_part`, `write_amendment_part`, `undo_part` — the brand-new part-write machinery from 3d952036/f9e70385)
- [store/query.rs L178, L216](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/store/query.rs) (`add_edge`/`remove_edge`)

The new part-write paths reproduce the defect class this same ticket claims to have closed.

---

### Per-ticket verdicts

#### 1. [5a3d152c 5a3d152c-faf7-4d33-8a4e-7ed19cf6b142](memory-api/.ticket/tickets/5a3d152c-faf7-4d33-8a4e-7ed19cf6b142/ticket.toml) — parts storage, claimed 9/9 AC

|---|---|---|
| 1 (atomic part+manifest write) | pass (best-effort) | file lock (`acquire_lock`) wraps write in [ticket_fs.rs](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/storage/ticket_fs.rs#L426); no true crash-atomicity but no half-state path found |
| 2 (invalid core kind rejected) | **fail** | `classify_part_kind` in [parts.rs](memory-api/crates/ticket-api/src/model/parts.rs) is explicitly documented "Never fails: every string is a valid attachment kind." `EntityTypeSchema::validate_manifest` ([schema.rs](memory-api/crates/memory-api/src/model/schema.rs#L63)) only checks required fields — no core-kind rejection exists anywhere. No test for this AC found. |
| 3 (free-form round-trip) | pass | test `unknown_kind_part_round_trips_as_opaque_attachment` passes |
| 4 (duplicate kind, stable order) | pass | code + manifest ordering by `id`, not kind/index |
| 5 (legacy implicit objective) | pass | test `legacy_ticket_with_no_parts_table_loads_implicit_objective` passes; confirmed live on real tickets |
| 6 (orphan file surfaced) | pass | test `orphan_part_file_is_reported_not_silently_adopted` passes |
| 7 (test-api evidence per AC) | **fail** | Only one bulk execution (`exec-vt-ticket-parts-storage-model-20260730`) recorded, not per-criterion; and it targets `vt-ticket-parts-storage-model`, not the epic's own declared-required `vt-structured-ticket-entities-rust` (which has **zero** executions) |

**Overall: FAIL** — AC2 unimplemented, AC7 evidence gap.

#### 2. [3d952036 3d952036-efd4-4f36-a77f-6b7f5058a0a0](memory-api/.ticket/tickets/3d952036-efd4-4f36-a77f-6b7f5058a0a0/ticket.toml) — part-addressed writes, mandatory description_mode, claimed 7/7 AC

| 3 (part write never touches objective) | pass | code confirms isolated file writes; test `parts_are_addressed_by_id_not_kind_or_index` passes |

| 5 (compile-time missing-field error) | **fail as literally stated** | `UpdateTicketInput.description_mode`, `UpdateTicketBody.description_mode`, `UpdateArgs.description_mode` are all `Option<...>` in [types.rs (mcp)](memory-api/tools/mcp/ticket-mcp/src/server/types.rs#L170), [types.rs (http)](memory-api/tools/http/ticket-http/src/serve/handlers/tickets/types.rs#L134), [operations.rs (cli)](memory-api/tools/cli/ticket-cli/src/cli/args/operations.rs#L258). These compile and deserialize fine when omitted (`None`); rejection is a **runtime** check in `store.rs`, not a compile-time one. The practical protection exists, but the AC's specific claim is inaccurate. |
